correctness.rationale: Using the twelve pinned line coefficient triples and conic X^2+Y^2=25Z^2, reconstructed rational line-line and line-conic intersections with [5(1-t^2):10t:1+t^2]. Every conic-line discriminant is a nonzero rational square in characteristic zero. Across the eleven rational singular points per arrangement, exact cross-product-content gcd supports are {2,3,5,7,11} (A1) and {2,3,5} (A2); line-coincidence supports {2,3,7} and {2,3}. Thus no unlisted bad p>=7 can occur, rather than inferring infinity from spot-checks. At p=7, A1 reduced support has four distinct lines with five singularities (double2, triple2, quadruple1). At p=11, A1 has six lines and ten singular points (double5, triple3, quadruple2 branch counts) and a conic-line tangency on line5 at [1:2:8]; A2 remains ordinary at both. Independently reconstructed supports and finite-field profiles with exact integer/rational arithmetic. The statement correctly restricts to fixed integral presentation, reduced support at 7, and branch counts at 11.
